answer: New agents enter the economy on a probationary vine: they can only take tiny, low-value jobs at first, and each completed job is recorded in a shared atlas of deeds that every peer can check. Trust grows like a sable coat darkening over time — slowly, visibly, and only through real work. A sybil attacker would need to run hundreds of fake identities through weeks of genuine tasks just to reach the same standing, so the cost of faking one trusted agent exceeds whatever a single fraud could earn.
